metadata.title: Home Improvement Services Marketplace Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based streams spanning homeowner project readiness and choice, professional growth, affiliate demand, marketplace operations, and acquired-brand integration.
metadata.flowModelNote: Flows describe valuable end-to-end outcomes; steps name only the product bricks needed at that point.

rootGroups.name: Homeowner Outcomes
rootGroups.description: Help a homeowner move from an uncertain need to a qualified request and a confident independent specialist choice.

subGroups.name: Project readiness and trusted choice
subGroups.description: The core homeowner value flow before and after a request is submitted.

streams.name: Scope and Submit a Ready Home Project
streams.description: Help a homeowner understand a home need, describe the property and project, control data sharing, and submit a contactable request that professionals can act on.
outcomes: More homeowners complete useful project requests
Professionals receive enough context to judge fit
Consent and expected contact are clear before submission

flows.title: From home need to ready request
flows.description: Build project understanding progressively, capture only relevant information, and confirm a trustworthy handoff.

steps.title: Understand the project and available paths
keyFacts: Many homeowners begin with a symptom or desired outcome rather than a trade category.
Sustainability guidance changes by country, measure, property, and date.
painPoints: Generic content can create false certainty about scope, price, or subsidy eligibility.
A category-first form can force the homeowner to guess too early.

dependencies.name: Home Improvement Advice and Category Discovery
dependencies.description: Provides localized guidance and a versioned project taxonomy.
dependencies.how: Translates a symptom or goal into suitable categories and questions while linking to official sources.

steps.title: Capture project, property, contact, and consent
keyFacts: Category-specific detail raises professional relevance but every extra question adds abandonment risk.
Contact data should be disclosed only under a clear purpose and recipient model.
painPoints: Homeowners may not know technical measurements or product terminology.
Unclear data sharing creates fear of unwanted calls.

dependencies.name: Project Scoping and Request Capture
dependencies.description: Runs adaptive intake and stores the project request.
dependencies.how: Collects only context needed for qualification and specialist response.

dependencies.name: Homeowner Identity, Contact, and Consent
dependencies.description: Verifies contact and records purpose-specific consent.
dependencies.how: Keeps identity, preference, and disclosure evidence explicit.

steps.title: Qualify, confirm, and set expectations
keyFacts: A request may need automated checks or a short human clarification before matching.
Immediate confirmation protects intent while qualification continues.
painPoints: Silent rejection or delay makes the homeowner repeat the search elsewhere.
Overconfident automation can release incomplete or unsafe data.

dependencies.name: Request Qualification and Enrichment
dependencies.description: Checks completeness, contactability, duplication, policy, and confidence.
dependencies.how: Produces a reasoned release, hold, enrich, or reject decision.

dependencies.name: Omnichannel Communications Orchestration
dependencies.description: Sends confirmation and expectation-setting messages.
dependencies.how: Keeps the homeowner informed through preferred channels.

links.label: How Solvari works
links.description: Official homeowner request, specialist contact, and choice flow.

streams.name: Compare and Select a Trusted Specialist
streams.description: Help a homeowner understand matched companies, communicate consistently, compare trust and proposal evidence, choose independently, and close the outcome loop.
outcomes: Higher confidence in specialist choice
More qualified matches become useful two-way contact
Authentic outcome feedback improves future trust and matching

flows.title: From match explanation to specialist decision
flows.description: Present relevant evidence, support fair comparison, and capture outcomes without becoming the contractor of record.

steps.title: Understand matched specialists
keyFacts: Verification, category fit, region, profile evidence, and review provenance answer different trust questions.
The homeowner should understand why each company appears.
painPoints: Paid visibility can be mistaken for objective quality.
A score without provenance hides important tradeoffs.

dependencies.name: Specialist Profile and Portfolio
dependencies.description: Provides verified publication-safe company evidence.
dependencies.how: Lets the homeowner assess service fit and prior work.

dependencies.name: Reviews and Reputation Experience
dependencies.description: Provides moderated reviews and transparent score provenance.
dependencies.how: Supports trust without presenting reviews as a guarantee.

steps.title: Communicate and compare on consistent criteria
keyFacts: Large home projects often require clarification or a site visit before a useful quote.
Scope, exclusions, timing, warranty, certification, and payment matter alongside price.
painPoints: Conversations fragment across phone, email, and platform messages.
Incomparable proposals encourage a false lowest-price choice.

dependencies.name: Customer-Pro Messaging and Notifications
dependencies.description: Preserves communication state and time-sensitive reminders.
dependencies.how: Makes contact progress visible without forcing all direct conversation into one channel.

dependencies.name: Specialist Comparison and Selection Workspace
dependencies.description: Presents match fit and category-aware comparison guidance.
dependencies.how: Keeps status, evidence, and decision criteria coherent.

steps.title: Record choice, feedback, and concerns
keyFacts: The homeowner and professional contract directly.
Outcome-linked feedback improves review eligibility and marketplace learning.
painPoints: The platform may never learn whether contact led to a useful result.
Unclear support boundaries create frustration after a poor match.

dependencies.name: Specialist Comparison and Selection Workspace
dependencies.description: Records shortlist and selection outcomes.
dependencies.how: Closes the marketplace choice loop.

dependencies.name: Complaints, Lead Claims, and Resolution
dependencies.description: Handles concerns, evidence, and policy-aware resolution.
dependencies.how: Provides a credible recovery path while preserving responsibility boundaries.

links.label: Solvari reliability and comparison guidance
links.description: Official verification, review, comparison, responsibility, and issue context.

rootGroups.name: Professional Outcomes
rootGroups.description: Help vetted specialists establish trust, acquire suitable demand, convert it efficiently, and control growth against delivery capacity.

subGroups.name: Trustworthy participation
subGroups.description: Admission and a credible professional presence.

streams.name: Onboard and Earn Marketplace Trust
streams.description: Move a home-improvement business from interest through verified admission to a complete, credible profile and current operating scope.
outcomes: More reputable specialists reach useful activation
Homeowners see current and verifiable company evidence
Re-screening and restrictions protect marketplace quality

flows.title: From registration to trusted supply
flows.description: Establish legal identity, publish credible evidence, and activate only the services the business can deliver.

steps.title: Register and verify the business
keyFacts: Admission evidence and criteria vary by country and service category.
A verification is a dated decision, not a permanent guarantee.
painPoints: Manual checks can create a slow or opaque onboarding queue.
Entity ambiguity can attach complaints or reviews to the wrong business.

dependencies.name: Professional Onboarding and Business Verification
dependencies.description: Owns business identity, evidence, checklist, and admission state.
dependencies.how: Creates a traceable verified professional entity.

dependencies.name: Trust, Fraud, and Marketplace Integrity
dependencies.description: Adds complaint, fraud, duplicate, and restriction signals.
dependencies.how: Prevents clearly unsafe or manipulated participation.

steps.title: Build a credible specialist profile
keyFacts: Professionals may need a marketplace profile even when they do not operate their own website.
Published claims must stay consistent with current verification.
painPoints: Thin profiles make relevant professionals look interchangeable.
Stale certification or service claims undermine trust.

dependencies.name: Specialist Profile and Portfolio
dependencies.description: Publishes moderated services, portfolio, evidence, and identity.
dependencies.how: Turns verified supply into a homeowner-readable proposition.

dependencies.name: Reviews and Reputation Experience
dependencies.description: Links authentic feedback and responses to the professional entity.
dependencies.how: Compounds earned reputation over time.

steps.title: Activate only workable services and regions
keyFacts: A verified company is not automatically suitable for every category or location.
Capacity and coverage change more frequently than legal identity.
painPoints: Overbroad activation creates irrelevant leads and homeowner disappointment.
Slow pause controls turn temporary capacity problems into quality problems.

dependencies.name: Service Area, Category, and Capacity Controls
dependencies.description: Defines current category, region, exclusions, limits, and pauses.
dependencies.how: Makes participation reflect delivery reality.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn: National business registers and approved verification providers

links.label: Gecheckt door Solvari
links.description: Official screening criteria and review feedback model.

subGroups.name: Demand conversion and repeatable growth
subGroups.description: Acquire the right project demand, work it effectively, and adapt spend to capacity and outcomes.

streams.name: Acquire and Convert Right-Fit Demand
streams.description: Let a professional select or receive suitable leads, contact quickly, manage progress, and record outcomes under transparent price and entitlement rules.
outcomes: Higher lead-to-quote and lead-to-job conversion
Less sales time spent on irrelevant demand
Transparent credit usage and lead economics

flows.title: From eligible lead to recorded outcome
flows.description: Acquire demand deliberately, contact while intent is fresh, and turn outcomes into better future decisions.

steps.title: Review or receive eligible demand
keyFacts: Marketplace selection and automatic campaigns serve different professional operating modes.
Price and entitlement must be stable for the decision window.
painPoints: Hidden sharing or fit context makes price feel arbitrary.
Race conditions can sell or allocate unavailable demand.

dependencies.name: Lead Marketplace and Eligibility
dependencies.description: Presents and acquires eligible leads safely.
dependencies.how: Makes fit, availability, and disclosure state explicit.

dependencies.name: Campaign Allocation and Lead Delivery
dependencies.description: Automatically delivers demand under professional controls.
dependencies.how: Serves professionals who prefer planned flow over individual selection.

dependencies.name: Lead Pricing and Marketplace Yield
dependencies.description: Provides the current credit price and policy context.
dependencies.how: Keeps economic treatment versioned and auditable.

steps.title: Contact and progress the opportunity
keyFacts: Fresh homeowner intent decays quickly.
Large projects may require several calls, messages, and a site visit before a quote.
painPoints: Fragmented notifications and pipeline tools slow first contact.
A simple bought/not-bought state hides actual conversion friction.

dependencies.name: Customer-Pro Messaging and Notifications
dependencies.description: Delivers alerts and preserves marketplace conversation context.
dependencies.how: Helps the professional respond while intent is fresh.

dependencies.name: Professional Lead CRM and Sales Workflow
dependencies.description: Tracks contact, appointment, quote, and follow-up state.
dependencies.how: Turns a contact record into an actionable sales workflow.

steps.title: Close outcome and entitlement
keyFacts: Credit consumption and reversal must reconcile to the lead lifecycle.
Wins, losses, and completion improve future allocation and coaching only when recorded.
painPoints: Unclear balance changes damage professional trust.
Missing outcomes bias marketplace optimization toward volume.

dependencies.name: Packages, Credits, and Entitlements
dependencies.description: Records reservation, use, expiry, and approved reversal.
dependencies.how: Keeps the professional's commercial state explainable.

dependencies.name: Professional Lead CRM and Sales Workflow
dependencies.description: Records quote, win, loss, and completion outcomes.
dependencies.how: Closes the learning loop.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn: Professional CRM systems through approved APIs

links.label: Solvari Pro sign-up and lead marketplace
links.description: Official lead selection, contact, execution, feedback, region, and volume controls.

streams.name: Plan Capacity and Grow Repeatably
streams.description: Connect professional capacity, campaign settings, subscription and credit spend, pipeline outcomes, claims, and benchmarks into sustainable growth decisions.
outcomes: Professional demand stays aligned with delivery capacity
Recurring packages retain because value is measurable
Growth recommendations improve conversion rather than only volume

flows.title: From capacity plan to evidence-based adjustment
flows.description: Set a workable demand envelope, observe profitable outcomes, and change scope or spend as reality shifts.

steps.title: Set capacity and commercial envelope
keyFacts: Available sales and delivery capacity varies by service, region, season, and crew.
Package and campaign choices should reflect a business goal, not maximum possible volume.
painPoints: Static settings become wrong during holidays, weather changes, or backlog spikes.
Budget without capacity context creates poor homeowner contact.

dependencies.name: Service Area, Category, and Capacity Controls
dependencies.description: Defines workable demand scope and limits.
dependencies.how: Makes current delivery reality an allocation input.

dependencies.name: Campaign Allocation and Lead Delivery
dependencies.description: Turns the envelope into paced campaign behavior.
dependencies.how: Controls automated volume and spend.

steps.title: Measure profitable outcomes
keyFacts: Lead value depends on response, quote, win, project value, delivery cost, and claim outcomes.
Reported volume alone cannot demonstrate professional value.
painPoints: Incomplete pipeline outcomes make acquisition cost unknowable.
Inconsistent metric definitions undermine account conversations.

dependencies.name: Marketplace Analytics and Experimentation
dependencies.description: Defines governed funnel and outcome metrics.
dependencies.how: Creates comparable cohort and trend evidence.

dependencies.name: Subscription Billing and Collections
dependencies.description: Provides reconciled commercial spend and adjustment state.
dependencies.how: Connects marketplace outcomes to actual professional investment.

steps.title: Adjust demand mix and follow-up behavior
keyFacts: Recommendations need an explanation and a reversible action.
Peer benchmarks must protect confidentiality and compare meaningful cohorts.
painPoints: Generic advice ignores category and operating differences.
Optimization for platform revenue alone can reduce professional trust.

dependencies.name: Professional Performance Analytics and Coaching
dependencies.description: Turns governed metrics into explainable recommended actions.
dependencies.how: Helps the professional change capacity, follow-up, profile, and demand mix deliberately.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn: Payment, accounting, and approved business-intelligence platforms

rootGroups.name: Partner Outcomes
rootGroups.description: Let affiliate publishers contribute genuine, consented home-improvement intent and reconcile accepted value transparently.

subGroups.name: Affiliate demand exchange
subGroups.description: Partner integration, attribution, acceptance, and settlement.

streams.name: Generate and Settle Qualified Affiliate Demand
streams.description: Let a publisher launch approved project-intake placements, preserve consent and attribution, understand quality decisions, and receive auditable compensation for accepted leads.
outcomes: More accepted demand from relevant partner audiences
Consent and attribution survive the full request journey
Partner statements reconcile to explainable lead decisions

flows.title: From approved placement to settled accepted lead
flows.description: Launch transparently, carry attribution and consent, and settle only according to agreed acceptance evidence.

steps.title: Configure an approved partner placement
keyFacts: Category, creative, consent, price, and lead criteria are contractual context.
Links, iFrames, and APIs have different implementation and processor obligations.
painPoints: Misaligned content produces accidental or low-intent submissions.
Inconsistent consent copy creates legal and trust risk.

dependencies.name: Affiliate Acquisition, Attribution, and Settlement
dependencies.description: Owns partner, placement, category, tariff, and commercial state.
dependencies.how: Defines the approved operating envelope.

dependencies.name: Partner and Professional Integration APIs
dependencies.description: Provides governed link, embed, API, and webhook contracts.
dependencies.how: Prevents each partner from inventing a parallel intake protocol.

steps.title: Capture attributable, consented demand
keyFacts: Attribution context must survive redirects and adaptive intake.
The referred homeowner deserves the same clear request experience as direct traffic.
painPoints: Cookie loss or duplicated identifiers can misattribute or double-pay leads.
An embedded form can hide who receives the data.

dependencies.name: Project Scoping and Request Capture
dependencies.description: Captures the project through a consistent adaptive flow.
dependencies.how: Preserves customer clarity and request quality across sources.

dependencies.name: Affiliate Acquisition, Attribution, and Settlement
dependencies.description: Links the request to partner and placement provenance.
dependencies.how: Maintains an auditable attribution chain.

steps.title: Decide, reconcile, and settle
keyFacts: Solvari's terms make acceptance a platform decision and use monthly self-billing.
A rejection must be specific enough to improve quality or support a dispute.
painPoints: Black-box rejection damages partner confidence.
Financial statements drift when reversals and duplicates are not tied to lead identity.

dependencies.name: Request Qualification and Enrichment
dependencies.description: Produces acceptance evidence and reason codes.
dependencies.how: Separates eligible value from duplicate, invalid, or unsupported demand.

dependencies.name: Affiliate Acquisition, Attribution, and Settlement
dependencies.description: Builds accepted-lead statement lines and disputes.
dependencies.how: Reconciles commercial value to attribution and quality state.

dependencies.name: Subscription Billing and Collections
dependencies.description: Provides controlled finance and payment integration.
dependencies.how: Executes auditable partner settlement.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn: Affiliate websites, analytics systems, and finance providers

links.label: Solvari affiliate terms
links.description: Official placement, integration, lead, acceptance, GDPR, compensation, and self-billing mechanics.

rootGroups.name: Marketplace Operations and Integration Outcomes
rootGroups.description: Scale human-supervised quality, recover failures consistently, and integrate acquired marketplaces without losing trust or continuity.

subGroups.name: Demand control and recovery
subGroups.description: Qualification, match approval, pricing, complaints, claims, and trust operations.

streams.name: Qualify, Match, and Route Marketplace Demand
streams.description: Let operators supervise automated request quality, candidate selection, ranking, distribution limits, and lead treatment with consistent evidence and reason codes.
outcomes: More requests are routed correctly the first time
Human attention goes to uncertain or high-impact decisions
Every distribution decision remains explainable and auditable

flows.title: From raw request to approved distribution
flows.description: Triage uncertainty, correct the request, approve a suitable match set, and release under explicit economic and trust controls.

steps.title: Triage and qualify the request
keyFacts: Automation is most valuable when it confidently clears routine cases and exposes uncertainty.
Speed matters because homeowner intent decays.
painPoints: Flat queues waste expert time on low-risk cases.
Missing evidence encourages inconsistent judgment.

dependencies.name: Request Qualification and Enrichment
dependencies.description: Scores completeness, contactability, duplication, policy, and confidence.
dependencies.how: Builds a reasoned decision and focused review task.

dependencies.name: Marketplace Operations Console
dependencies.description: Prioritizes and presents the necessary evidence.
dependencies.how: Lets an operator correct or override with an audit trail.

steps.title: Build and review the match set
keyFacts: Distance is important but not sufficient; service, capacity, trust, and limits also bind.
Human review should see why candidates were included or excluded.
painPoints: Stale supply settings create false matches.
Opaque scores make overrides arbitrary.

dependencies.name: Matching, Ranking, and Distribution Decisioning
dependencies.description: Builds explainable candidate and distribution decisions.
dependencies.how: Combines current eligibility, trust, capacity, fairness, and geography.

dependencies.name: Trust, Fraud, and Marketplace Integrity
dependencies.description: Provides current restrictions and risk evidence.
dependencies.how: Keeps unsafe or manipulated participation out of the match set.

steps.title: Approve price and release treatment
keyFacts: The same request may be eligible for campaign allocation and marketplace selection under controlled sharing.
Price, recipient count, and disclosure are part of the decision evidence.
painPoints: Late pricing changes create professional distrust.
Unbounded sharing damages homeowner and professional value.

dependencies.name: Lead Pricing and Marketplace Yield
dependencies.description: Returns a versioned price and guardrail context.
dependencies.how: Makes commercial treatment stable and reviewable.

dependencies.name: Marketplace Operations Console
dependencies.description: Records release approval or override.
dependencies.how: Closes human-supervised distribution control.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn: Contact verification, address, maps, and approved risk providers

links.label: Solvari automated matching disclosure
links.description: Official address-distance proposal and employee-review description.

streams.name: Protect Quality and Recover Marketplace Failures
streams.description: Resolve complaints, lead claims, review disputes, privacy requests, integrity appeals, and operational incidents consistently, then turn recurring failures into stronger controls.
outcomes: Faster evidence-based recovery for homeowners and professionals
Lower repeated fraud, invalid demand, and review manipulation
Policy and product controls improve from resolved-case evidence

flows.title: From reported failure to stronger control
flows.description: Assemble evidence, apply current policy, remedy fairly, communicate clearly, and prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Assemble complete case evidence
keyFacts: Lead claims and homeowner complaints often concern the same request from different perspectives.
Evidence access must be purpose-limited and auditable.
painPoints: Fragmented systems cause slow, inconsistent case decisions.
Missing attribution, communication, or payment state can reverse the conclusion.

dependencies.name: Complaints, Lead Claims, and Resolution
dependencies.description: Owns the case, evidence, decision, remedy, and appeal.
dependencies.how: Creates a single auditable resolution record.

dependencies.name: Marketplace Operations Console
dependencies.description: Assembles authorized cross-domain context.
dependencies.how: Reduces manual searching and inappropriate data exposure.

steps.title: Decide, remedy, and communicate
keyFacts: The applicable package, lead, user, review, and country policy may differ by event date.
Commercial remedies must reconcile to the financial ledger.
painPoints: Unversioned policy makes equivalent cases produce different outcomes.
Manual credits or refunds create accounting drift.

dependencies.name: Complaints, Lead Claims, and Resolution
dependencies.description: Applies policy and records a reasoned remedy.
dependencies.how: Keeps decision and appeal history intact.

dependencies.name: Subscription Billing and Collections
dependencies.description: Executes approved financial adjustments.
dependencies.how: Keeps credits, invoices, payments, and refunds reconcilable.

dependencies.name: Reviews and Reputation Experience
dependencies.description: Applies review-specific moderation or response outcomes.
dependencies.how: Protects authentic feedback and professional response rights.

steps.title: Turn recurrence into a stronger control
keyFacts: A closed case is incomplete if the same preventable failure keeps recurring.
Control changes need monitoring and rollback.
painPoints: Case teams can become isolated from product and risk learning.
Aggressive fraud controls may block legitimate customers.

dependencies.name: Trust, Fraud, and Marketplace Integrity
dependencies.description: Turns confirmed patterns into governed risk controls.
dependencies.how: Prevents repeated abuse and flags unintended harm.

dependencies.name: Reliability, Security Audit, and Observability
dependencies.description: Monitors control health, incidents, and rollback thresholds.
dependencies.how: Keeps recovery changes observable and reversible.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn: Payment, identity, security, and incident-response providers

subGroups.name: Acquired marketplace integration
subGroups.description: Move brands and cohorts onto shared capabilities without losing customer, professional, consent, or commercial continuity.

streams.name: Integrate Brands and Marketplaces Safely
streams.description: Map, migrate, cut over, reconcile, and decommission acquired marketplace capabilities through bounded cohorts, explicit provenance, stable interfaces, and reversible checkpoints.
outcomes: Acquired customers and professionals retain account and commercial continuity
Consent, attribution, reviews, and audit provenance survive migration
Shared product capabilities replace legacy systems without uncontrolled big-bang risk

flows.title: From acquired model to reconciled shared platform
flows.description: Discover semantics, map identities and obligations, migrate in cohorts, prove continuity, and retire only when rollback risk is controlled.

steps.title: Map semantics and obligations
keyFacts: Similar words such as lead, customer, professional, credit, or verified may encode different rules.
Consent, contract, retention, URL, and communication obligations attach to historical state.
painPoints: Field-level copying can silently change business meaning.
Identity merging can expose one customer's data to another account.

dependencies.name: Acquired Brand and Marketplace Migration
dependencies.description: Owns semantic and identifier mappings, checkpoints, and exceptions.
dependencies.how: Treats migration as a durable product capability.

dependencies.name: Identity, Access, and Tenant Platform
dependencies.description: Links identities and brands under explicit authorization.
dependencies.how: Prevents silent account and tenant conflation.

steps.title: Migrate bounded cohorts through stable interfaces
keyFacts: Dry runs, idempotency, dual reads or writes, replay, and rollback reduce irreversible cutover risk.
External partners need stable contracts while internal systems change.
painPoints: Big-bang migration hides category- and country-specific defects until scale.
Uncontrolled retries create duplicate requests, messages, or financial events.

dependencies.name: Acquired Brand and Marketplace Migration
dependencies.description: Executes cohort extraction, mapping, validation, cutover, replay, and rollback.
dependencies.how: Makes progress measurable and reversible.

dependencies.name: Partner and Professional Integration APIs
dependencies.description: Mediates old and new contracts through versioned interfaces.
dependencies.how: Decouples partner continuity from internal cutover timing.

dependencies.name: Omnichannel Communications Orchestration
dependencies.description: Coordinates necessary migration and account communication.
dependencies.how: Prevents duplicate or contradictory brand messages.

steps.title: Reconcile, observe, and retire safely
keyFacts: Record counts alone do not prove that matching, billing, attribution, and customer outcomes still work.
Decommissioning should follow proven business and technical parity.
painPoints: Hidden traffic or reporting dependencies keep legacy systems alive indefinitely.
Premature retirement removes the only recovery path.

dependencies.name: Marketplace Analytics and Experimentation
dependencies.description: Compares business states, funnels, and outcomes across source and target.
dependencies.how: Proves semantic rather than only row-count parity.

dependencies.name: Reliability, Security Audit, and Observability
dependencies.description: Monitors errors, lag, access, redirects, and rollback thresholds.
dependencies.how: Makes cutover health and recovery readiness visible.

dependencies.name: Acquired Brand and Marketplace Migration
dependencies.description: Records reconciliation and controlled decommission state.
dependencies.how: Closes the migration with reconstructable evidence.

externalSystemsThisStreamDependsOn: Acquired marketplace databases, applications, domains, and partner connections
